title: Candidate Evidence → Impact: Blueprint for Technical Hires
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a compact, evidence-driven path from candidate evaluation to measurable impact for individual contributor (IC) and engineering lead hires. The goal is to reduce guesswork in hiring, shorten time-to-first-impact, and standardize manager obligations for ramp and early feedback. Use this blueprint for senior engineers through staff+ and for early-career mid-level ICs where consistent ramp expectations are required.

Principles
----------
- Evidence-first: every hire decision is supported by scored artifacts (take-home, live coding rubric, work sample, reference notes).
- Time-boxed checkpoints: clear 30/60/90 and autonomy criteria for both hiring and onboarding.
- Manager accountability: hiring managers own interview packets, the first 90 days, and the probation calibration.
- Measurable outcomes: define 3 impact signals that show early contribution (examples below).

1) Hiring process: evidence checklist and SLAs
------------------------------------------------
Purpose: ensure consistent, fast, and fair evaluation for technical roles.

Required artifacts per candidate (attach to interview packet):
- Resume + role-fit statement (1–2 sentences from recruiter)
- Work sample or public repo links (if provided)
- Take-home assessment (scored with rubric) OR structured pair-programming session notes
- Interview feedback forms (one per interviewer, scored 1–5 on core competencies)
- Reference check summary (template-based)

Pipeline SLAs (goal targets):
1. Recruiter screen → on-site/loop scheduled: 7 business days
2. Final onsite → written offer: 5 business days
3. Offer acceptance → start date coordination: 10 business days

Decision rubric (mandatory fields in every packet):
- Technical proficiency (design, algorithmic thinking, system tradeoffs) — score 1–5
- Code craft (readability, testing, maintainability) — score 1–5
- Collaboration & communication — score 1–5
- Ownership & impact exemplars — score 1–5
- Role-fit & domain knowledge — score 1–5
- Hiring manager overall recommendation — hire / hire-with-conditions / no-hire

Hiring committee gating rules:
- At least 4 interviewers with independent feedback for senior roles.
- No hire unless median technical proficiency >= 3 and hiring manager recommendation != 'no-hire'.
- Any single interview score of 1 requires a synchronous calibration conversation before progressing.

2) Offer & acceptance: negotiation guardrails
-------------------------------------------
- Team owners: hiring manager + finance-approved banding owner
- Typical negotiation window: 72 hours for non-executive offers. Extenuating circumstances escalate to People Ops.
- Equity/grant guidance: provide a 4-year vesting schedule memo and examples of target total comp for comparable roles.

3) First-week onboarding checklist (manager + buddy responsibilities)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Manager (to complete by EOW):
- 1:1 scheduled cadence (weekly for first 12 weeks) + 30/60/90 syncs added to calendar
- Technical orientation: architecture tour, key repo access, dev workstation checklist completed
- Contribute mini-ticket: small scoped task assigned with acceptance criteria (goal: first merged PR by day 10)
- Security & access: confirm SSO, VPN, KMS access where applicable
- Intro emails to cross-functional partners

Buddy (peer) responsibilities:
- Daily shadowing for first 3 business days, then as-needed pairing for first 2 weeks
- Walkthrough of local dev loops, CI/CD, test environments

Checklist table (text format)
Item | Owner | Target
-----|-------|-------
Workstation provisioned | IT/infra | Day 0
Core repo access | Manager | Day 1
First PR assigned | Manager | Day 3
First PR merged | New hire + reviewer | Day 10
Documentation tour | Buddy | Day 3
Security training completed | New hire | Day 5

4) 30/60/90 and probation signals for measurable early impact
-------------------------------------------------------------
Define 3 impact signals at offer stage and include them in the new hire packet. Examples:
- Signal A: First meaningful PR merged to a production-adjacent service with approvals and passing CI (metric: merged by day 14).
- Signal B: Owned bug fix with post-deploy monitoring and incident notes written (metric: completed with postmortem by day 45).
- Signal C: Documented design note or RFC that is adopted or requested changes implemented (metric: doc produced by day 60).

30-day check-in (manager):
- Focus: fundamentals, access, team rituals.
- Artifacts: list of completed onboarding tasks, first PR diff, interview-style quick calibration from two dev peers.
- Outcome: continue / escalate support / role re-scope.

60-day check-in (manager):
- Focus: scoped ownership and cross-team collaboration.
- Artifacts: evidence of Signal A or equivalent.
- Outcome: on-track / needs focused coaching / probation plan.

90-day (probation end) calibration:
- Formal review: manager writes a 360-style recommendation with peer input and hiring packet attached.
- Criteria for pass: at least two signals achieved OR documented progress on a written improvement plan with objective milestones.

5) Manager guide: concrete nudges and feedback templates
-------------------------------------------------------
Manager responsibilities timeline (first 12 weeks):
- Week 0–1: logistics, dev environment, assign buddy, set first PR
- Week 2–4: weekly 1:1s focused on blockers, code reviews, and early wins
- Week 4–8: start delegation of small feature/bug scope; ensure cross-team introductions
- Week 8–12: align on 90-day deliverable; begin performance calibration notes for probation decision

Feedback templates (use in 1:1 and calibration):
- Quick check-in (weekly): "What went well this week? What blocked you? What support do you need?"
- Development ask (when coaching): "Action: do X. Expected outcome: Y. Follow-up date: DD/MM."
- Calibration summary (90 days): "Evidence: [PRs, docs, tickets]. Recommendation: Pass / Extend probation (30d) / Exit. Rationale: [3 bullets]."

6) Performance & compensation cadence tie-ins
--------------------------------------------
- New hires enter normal cycle but are flagged for early calibration in the next full-cycle review batch if hire date is within 60 days.
- Compensation adjustments within the first 12 months follow existing promotion/comp change policies; managers must submit change requests with documented impact artifacts.

7) Remediation and extension process (probation extensions)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Trigger: 90-day check results in 'Extend probation'
- Extension length: 30 days (standard) or 60 days (case justification required)
- Elements of extension plan: clear success criteria (2–3 metrics), weekly 1:1 cadence, mentor assigned, HR check-ins every 2 weeks
- Final decision: hiring manager + people-ops lead + one calibration reviewer within 5 business days of extension end

8) Interviewer training & bias mitigation
----------------------------------------
Mandatory interviewer prep materials:
- Structured rubric PDF (required)
- Example scored assessments with commentary
- 60-minute bias training + calibration session per quarter for all interviewers on the panel list

Bias mitigation rules:
- No single interviewer veto beyond documented low score process (see Hiring committee gating rules).
- Use anonymized take-home coding whitelists where possible for junior roles.
- Calibrate scoring monthly with a synthetic candidate exercise; results are published to the hiring org.

9) Metrics & dashboards (what we track)
---------------------------------------
- Time-to-offer (median days) — target: <= 12 days
- Acceptance rate by band — target: >= 70%
- First-PR-merge rate by day 14 — target: >= 80% for mid/senior ICs
- 90-day pass rate — target: >= 90%
- Interviewer variance (std dev of scores across panel) — target: <= 1.2

Ownership: People Ops owns metrics dashboard; hiring managers own per-candidate hiring packet completeness.

Appendices
----------
A. Example 30/60/90 template (paste into offer packet)
- 30-day goals: access, small PR merged, setup local env, meet cross-functional partners
- 60-day goals: take ownership of a subcomponent, propose 1 design improvement, close 3 bugs/features
- 90-day goals: lead a design review, ship a measurable change, document handoff notes

B. Take-home assessment scoring snapshot (example rubric)
- Correctness (0–40)
- Design & scalability (0–25)
- Tests & edge cases (0–15)
- Readability & docs (0–10)
- Execution & delivery (time/clarity) (0–10)

C. Quick manager checklist (one-pager)
- Ensure packet complete before offer sign-off
- Schedule weekly 1:1s and 30/60/90 syncs
- Assign buddy and first PR by day 3
- Set clear success signals in writing at offer stage

Contacts and escalation
----------------------
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (case coordinator for offers, extensions, and calibration requests)
- Compensation owner: finance-legal-comp@redwood.com
- Interviewer training owner: talent-development@redwood.com
